findings.passage: The office will produce a professional training curriculum — video modules and printed materials, customized to the specific voting systems used across Indiana's counties — covering the issues that come up over and over: acceptable voter ID, provisional ballots, electioneering rules, chain-of-custody paperwork, and keeping lines moving without cutting corners.
findings.note: Campaign plan page (same text is in the dated post of 9 Sep 2026 at https://gregballard.com/greg-ballards-plan-to-safeguard-indiana-elections/). Lists acceptable voter ID and provisional ballots as topics for a standard poll worker training course. Does not say what the ID rule should be.
subjects: poll worker training on ID rules

findings.passage: Bring a photo ID. Indiana law requires a photo ID issued by the State of Indiana or the U.S. government.
findings.note: Campaign-issued demonstration voters guide (Boone County sample, labelled with a note from Ballard). States the current Indiana photo ID rule as information for voters. Date is the PDF creation date in its file data.

findings.passage: You must still be offered a provisional ballot. To have it counted, take a valid photo ID to the county election board by noon on Friday, November 13 — ten days after the election. If you have a religious objection to being photographed, or cannot afford an ID, sign an affidavit at that office by the same deadline instead.
findings.note: Same campaign voters guide, under 'If your photo ID is refused'. Describes the current provisional ballot and affidavit route for a voter without acceptable ID. Informational text, not a proposal.

findings.passage: Voters who registered after January 1, 2006 and have not yet voted in Indiana must give the county one more document proving where they live: a photo ID, or a utility bill, bank statement, government check, paycheck, or other government document showing your name at your registration address.
findings.note: Same campaign voters guide. Explains the current document rule for first-time voters, including non-photo documents such as a utility bill. Informational text.
subjects: non-photo documents such as a utility bill

findings.passage: I'll only promise what this office can deliver. The Secretary of State runs Indiana's elections, handles business filings, and regulates securities. We will not be asking for federal legislation that interferes with Indiana’s ability to run its own elections, nor will we talk about other issues where the Secretary of State has no control.
findings.note: Campaign pledge in a release issued in his name. Related: says he will not ask for federal election legislation and will keep to matters the office controls. Does not name voter ID or the SAVE Act.

subjects: documentary proof of citizenship / SAVE Act
